hero.title: Why is losing weight so difficult?
hero.subtitle: And are Ozempic or Mounjaro the right choices for you? Complete information in simple language.

section2.title: Why is losing weight so hard?
section2.intro: Our bodies were not built for today's food environment.
section2.thenText: In the past, food was scarce, so the body evolved to save energy (store fat).
section2.nowText: Today food is abundant, but the body's programming remains the same.
section2.analogyText: “Just like an inverter goes into power save mode when power fails, the body slows down metabolism when you diet.”

section3.title: How hunger and hormones work?
section3.intro: Our body signals hunger and fullness through specific hormones.
section3.cardTitle: What is GLP-1 and how does it work?
section3.explanation: “GLP-1 signals the brain from the gut that the stomach is full.”

section4.title: What are Ozempic and Mounjaro?
section4.intro: Both are weekly injections that reduce appetite and improve sugar control.
section4.ozempicDesc: Works like the GLP-1 hormone. It reduces hunger and helps with sugar control.
section4.mounjaroDesc: Mimics both GLP-1 + GIP hormones. It can be even more effective than Ozempic.

section5.title: Side Effects (Explained Honestly)
section5.intro: Every medicine has some side effects, and so do these. But with right information, they can be managed.
section5.commonDesc: Nausea, Vomiting, Constipation, Stomach pain, Acidity. These are usually temporary and the body adjusts slowly.
section5.seriousDesc: Pancreatitis, Gallbladder problem, Thyroid tumor risk (seen in animals, rare in humans).
section5.doseTitle: Why is the dose increased slowly?
section5.doseDesc: To minimize side effects, doctors always start with a low dose and increase it week by week. This is called Titration.
section5.warningText: If you or your family has a history of Thyroid cancer (MTC) or MEN 2 syndrome, do not take these medicines. Talk to your doctor openly.

section6.title: Who is it right for?
section6.intro: This medicine is not for everyone. Doctors prescribe it only when weight-related diseases pose a risk.
qualifiesList: • BMI over 27 + Diabetes, BP, or Cholesterol
notForList: • Cosmetic weight loss (just to look good)
section6.consultText: Doctor's advice and prescription are mandatory. Do not self-medicate.

section7.title: It is not magic (Lifestyle Matters)
section7.intro: Medicine is just a support. If you don't change your lifestyle, weight can come back after stopping medicine.
section7.quote: “Medicine reduces hunger, but what to eat is your choice.”

section8.title: Cost and Considerations in India
section8.intro: These medicines are not cheap and may need to be taken for a long time.
section8.costDesc: Monthly cost can be ₹15,000 - ₹25,000+ (depending on brand and dose).
section8.timeDesc: This is not a 1-month course. You may need to take it for months or years on doctor's advice.
section8.insuranceDesc: Currently in India, most health insurance plans do not cover obesity medicines.

section9.title: Myths vs Truth
section9.intro: There are many misconceptions about weight in society. Let's know the truth.
section9.myth1: Just eat less and walk, weight will go down.
section9.truth1: Obesity is a complex disease. Hormones (Biology) play a big role, not just willpower.
section9.myth2: Taking injections will ruin the body.
section9.truth2: Under doctor's supervision, these medicines can be safe and prevent many diseases (Diabetes, Heart).

section10.title: Take the Right Step (Compassionate Conclusion)
section10.lead: Losing weight is not just about willpower. It's a game of hormones and biology.
section10.body: New medicines can help, but right information and doctor's advice are most important. Prioritize your health and talk to a qualified doctor.
